claim: Chondrocyte columns play a central role in bone elongation.
source: Chondrocyte columns, which are a hallmark of growth plate architecture, play a central role in bone elongation.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a foundational concept for the study.

claim: Columns are formed by clonal expansion following rotation of the division plane, resulting in a stack of cells oriented parallel to the growth direction.
source: Columns are formed by clonal expansion following rotation of the division plane, resulting in a stack of cells oriented parallel to the growth direction.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established understanding of column formation.

claim: Most cells in embryonic growth plates did not display the typical stacking pattern associated with column formation.
source: Surprisingly, analysis of the elevation angles between neighboring pairs of cells revealed that most cells did not display the typical stacking pattern associated with column formation, implying incomplete rotation of the division plane.
evidence: This is a primary finding stated in the abstract based on the study's analysis.

claim: Incomplete rotation of the division plane occurs in embryonic growth plate cells.
source: Surprisingly, analysis of the elevation angles between neighboring pairs of cells revealed that most cells did not display the typical stacking pattern associated with column formation, implying incomplete rotation of the division plane.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation of non-typical stacking patterns.

claim: Embryonic clones were elongated.
source: Morphological analysis revealed that although embryonic clones were elongated, they formed clusters oriented perpendicular to the growth direction.
evidence: This is a finding from morphological analysis stated in the abstract.

claim: Embryonic clones formed clusters oriented perpendicular to the growth direction.
source: Morphological analysis revealed that although embryonic clones were elongated, they formed clusters oriented perpendicular to the growth direction.
evidence: This is a finding from morphological analysis stated in the abstract.

claim: Postnatal growth plates contain both complex columns composed of ordered and disordered cell stacks and small, disorganized clusters located in the outer edges.
source: Analysis of growth plates of postnatal mice revealed both complex columns, composed of ordered and disordered cell stacks, and small, disorganized clusters located in the outer edges.
evidence: This is a finding from analysis of postnatal growth plates stated in the abstract.

claim: Clusters may promote expansion, whereas columns support elongation.
source: Finally, correlation between the temporal dynamics of the ratios between clusters and columns and between bone elongation and expansion suggests that clusters may promote expansion, whereas columns support elongation.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion based on correlation analysis stated in the abstract.

claim: Modulations of division plane rotation of proliferating chondrocytes determines the formation of either clusters or columns.
source: Overall, our findings support the idea that modulations of division plane rotation of proliferating chondrocytes determines the formation of either clusters or columns, a multifunctional design that regulates morphogenesis throughout pre- and postnatal bone growth.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings stated in the abstract.

claim: The growth plate comprises four zones: resting zone (RZ), proliferative zone (PZ), prehypertrophic zone (PHZ), and hypertrophic zone (HZ).
source: The growth plate comprises four zones. At the most distal epiphyseal end is the resting zone (RZ), where chondrocytes are small and disorganized. Underneath lies the proliferative zone (PZ), where chondrocytes increase in volume, adopt a flat and elongated morphology, and organize into columns (Abad et al., 2002; Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Romereim et al., 2014). In the subsequent prehypertrophic (PHZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ), cells reach their maximum size (Rubin et al., 2021; Cooper et al., 2013; Breur et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge about growth plate structure cited from previous literature.

claim: In the resting zone, chondrocytes are small and disorganized.
source: At the most distal epiphyseal end is the resting zone (RZ), where chondrocytes are small and disorganized.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the resting zone.

claim: In the proliferative zone, chondrocytes increase in volume, adopt a flat and elongated morphology, and organize into columns.
source: Underneath lies the proliferative zone (PZ), where chondrocytes increase in volume, adopt a flat and elongated morphology, and organize into columns (Abad et al., 2002; Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Romereim et al., 2014).
evidence: This is established knowledge about the proliferative zone cited from previous literature.

claim: In the prehypertrophic and hypertrophic zones, cells reach their maximum size.
source: In the subsequent prehypertrophic (PHZ) and hypertrophic zones (HZ), cells reach their maximum size (Rubin et al., 2021; Cooper et al., 2013; Breur et al., 1997).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Changes in cell size and spatial organization determine the rate of bone elongation.
source: These changes in cell size and spatial organization determine the rate of bone elongation (Breur et al., 1991; Wilsman et al., 2008; Wilsman et al., 1996; Kember and Walker, 1971; Lui et al., 2018; Li et al., 2015).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Columnar arrangement of chondrocytes has been a subject of study for nearly a century.
source: Columnar arrangement of chondrocytes has been a subject of study for nearly a century (Dodds, 1930), gaining attention due to the remarkable emergence of cellular order from the highly disordered RZ.
evidence: This is a historical statement cited from Dodds, 1930.

claim: Columnar arrangement facilitates bone elongation by maximizing cell density in the longitudinal axis while limiting it laterally.
source: This columnar arrangement facilitates bone elongation by maximizing cell density in the longitudinal axis while limiting it laterally, thereby constraining hypertrophic cell growth to the P-D axis (Romereim and Dudley, 2011).
evidence: This is established understanding cited from previous literature.

claim: In the PZ, the division of column-forming cells is perpendicular to the P-D axis.
source: In the PZ, the division of column-forming cells is perpendicular to the P-D axis.
evidence: This is established knowledge about cell division orientation in the proliferative zone.

claim: Analyses of two-dimensional static images suggested that in the embryonic growth plate, columns form through a process akin to convergent extension.
source: Originally, analyses of two-dimensional static images suggested that in the embryonic growth plate, columns form through a process akin to convergent extension, an evolutionarily conserved tissue elongation mechanism involving cell intercalation (Li and Dudley, 2009; Ahrens et al., 2009; Shwartz et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2003).
evidence: This is a historical interpretation from previous studies cited in the text.

claim: Live imaging studies showed that cells do not intercalate to form columns.
source: However, more recent live imaging studies in various model systems showed that cells do not intercalate to form columns (Li et al., 2017; Romereim and Dudley, 2011; Yuan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is a finding from recent studies cited in the text.

claim: Following cell division, sister cells undergo a cell–cell and cell–extracellular matrix (ECM) adhesion-dependent 90° rotation prior to separation.
source: Instead, following cell division, sister cells undergo a cell–cell and cell–extracellular matrix (ECM) adhesion-dependent 90° rotation prior to separation.
evidence: This is established understanding from recent studies.

claim: Rotation ensures that cells are neatly stacked with their short axis parallel to the P-D axis.
source: This rotation ensures that cells are neatly stacked with their short axis parallel to the P-D axis.
evidence: This is established understanding of the function of rotation.

claim: Columns consist of clonal cells.
source: First, columns consist of clonal cells (Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Romereim et al., 2014; Ahrens et al., 2009; Newton et al., 2019; Mizuhashi et al., 2018; Hallett et al., 2022).
evidence: This is an established principle cited from previous literature.

claim: Embryonic columns are multiclonal.
source: Whereas embryonic columns are multiclonal, postnatally, following the formation of secondary ossification centers, columns become monoclonal and originate from Pthrp + RZ cells (Newton et al., 2019; Mizuhashi et al., 2018; Hallett et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Postnatally, following the formation of secondary ossification centers, columns become monoclonal and originate from Pthrp + RZ cells.
source: Whereas embryonic columns are multiclonal, postnatally, following the formation of secondary ossification centers, columns become monoclonal and originate from Pthrp + RZ cells (Newton et al., 2019; Mizuhashi et al., 2018; Hallett et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Cells within the column orient their short axis parallel to the P-D axis of the bone within a threshold of 12°.
source: The second principle is that cells within the column orient their short axis parallel to the P-D axis of the bone (Rubin et al., 2021; Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Romereim et al., 2014; Ahrens et al., 2009; Shwartz et al., 2012; Aszodi et al., 2003) within a threshold of 12° (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an established principle cited from previous literature.

claim: The long axis of the column is oriented parallel to the P-D axis within a 12° threshold for single columns and a 20° threshold for complex columns.
source: The long axis is oriented parallel to the P-D axis (Dodds, 1930; Li and Dudley, 2009; Romereim et al., 2014; Ahrens et al., 2009; Shwartz et al., 2012; Aszodi et al., 2003; Moss-Salentijn et al., 1987) within a 12° threshold for single columns and a 20° threshold for complex columns (Li et al., 2017).
evidence: This is an established principle cited from previous literature.

claim: Beta 1 and alpha 10 integrins, along with α-parvin, are physical regulators governing cell polarity and rotation during column formation.
source: Studies in embryonic and postnatal mouse limbs have shown the importance of interactions between chondrocytes and the surrounding ECM. These studies have identified beta 1 and alpha 10 integrins, along with α-parvin, as physical regulators governing cell polarity and rotation during column formation (Yuan et al., 2023; Aszodi et al., 2003; Bengtsson et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: The Fz/Vangl/PCP pathway plays a major role in regulating chondrocyte polarity and rearrangement.
source: Furthermore, studies in embryonic chick and mouse limbs have shown that cell surface signaling through the Fz/Vangl/PCP pathway plays a major role in regulating chondrocyte polarity and rearrangement (Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Ahrens et al., 2009; Gao et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2003; Yang and Mlodzik, 2015) and that GDF5 is involved in chondrocyte orientation (Rubin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: GDF5 is involved in chondrocyte orientation.
source: Furthermore, studies in embryonic chick and mouse limbs have shown that cell surface signaling through the Fz/Vangl/PCP pathway plays a major role in regulating chondrocyte polarity and rearrangement (Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Ahrens et al., 2009; Gao et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2003; Yang and Mlodzik, 2015) and that GDF5 is involved in chondrocyte orientation (Rubin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Muscle load plays an important role in regulating cell polarity and column formation.
source: Finally, studies in paralyzed mice (Killion et al., 2017) and muscle-less mouse embryos Shwartz et al., 2012; Pierantoni et al., 2021 have uncovered the important role of muscle load in regulating cell polarity and column formation.
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Chondrocytes in the embryonic growth plate are rarely arranged in columns.
source: Intriguingly, we found that chondrocytes in the embryonic growth plate are rarely arranged in columns.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study stated in the introduction.

claim: The low rates of complete division plane rotations suggest that the orientation of the division plane is tightly regulated.
source: Thus, the low rates of complete division plane rotations, deduced from the doublet elevation angle analysis, suggest that the orientation of the division plane is tightly regulated.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the study's findings and simulation results stated in the discussion.

claim: Previous work provides indications for both mechanical and molecular signals that regulate the rotation of the division plane, including Fz/Vangl/PCP signaling, integrins and muscle force, as well as matrix composition.
source: While the mechanisms that regulates the rotation of the division plane during bone growth are not fully understood, previous work provides several indications for both mechanical and molecular signals. These include Fz/Vangl/PCP signaling, integrins and muscle force, as well as matrix composition (Li and Dudley, 2009; Li et al., 2017; Ahrens et al., 2009; Shwartz et al., 2012; Gao et al., 2011; Yang et al., 2003; Yuan et al., 2023; Aszodi et al., 2003; Bengtsson et al., 2005; Yang and Mlodzik, 2015; Killion et al., 2017; Pierantoni et al., 2021; Kuss et al., 2014; Prein et al., 2016).
evidence: This is a summary of established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: Previous studies showed a switch in column clonality when the secondary ossification center forms.
source: Previous studies showed a switch in column clonality when the secondary ossification center forms (Newton et al., 2019; Mizuhashi et al., 2018; Hallett et al., 2022).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: It is reasonable to speculate that clones switch from orthogonally oriented clusters to parallel columns when the secondary ossification center forms.
source: Therefore, it is reasonable to speculate that clones switch from orthogonally oriented clusters to parallel columns at that time point.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: One limitation of the rotation analysis is that it was assumed that chondrocyte rotation and orientation are correlated and that chondrocytes do not move after rotating.
source: One limitation of our rotation analysis is that in order to calculate the relative position between neighboring cells, we assumed that chondrocyte rotation and orientation are correlated and that chondrocytes do not move after rotating, as was previously suggested (Romereim et al., 2014; Yuan et al., 2023).
evidence: This is an acknowledgment of a limitation stated in the discussion.

claim: Growth plates of various organisms employ different strategies to create bones of diverse morphologies, which serve different functions such as running, swimming, flying, etc.
source: Moreover. growth plates of various organisms employ different strategies to create bones of diverse morphologies, which serve different functions such as running, swimming, flying, etc.
evidence: This is a general statement about biological diversity stated in the discussion.

claim: It is possible that in each context, the ratio between clusters and columns is adjusted to cope with different functional requirements.
source: Thus, it is possible that in each context, the ratio between clusters and columns is adjusted to cope with these different requirements.
evidence: This is a speculative conclusion stated in the discussion.

claim: The core mechanism underlying chondrocyte column formation, namely a complete rotation of the division plane during chondrocyte proliferation, is rare in the embryonic growth plate.
source: Here, we discovered that the core mechanism underlying chondrocyte column formation, namely a complete rotation of the division plane during chondrocyte proliferation, is rare in the embryonic growth plate.
evidence: This is a summary of the main finding stated in the discussion.

claim: 3D analyses reveal the temporal dynamics of division plane rotations and their effect on the formation of columns and clusters in the pre- and postnatal growth plate.
source: Our 3D analyses reveal the temporal dynamics of division plane rotations and their effect on the formation of columns and clusters in the pre- and postnatal growth plate, as well as the correlation of these morphogenetic processes with different growth behaviors.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contributions stated in the discussion.

claim: These findings establish a new model for column formation and provide a new understanding of the cellular mechanisms underlying growth plate activity and bone elongation and expansion during development.
source: Overall, these findings establish a new model for column formation and provide a new understanding of the cellular mechanisms underlying growth plate activity and bone elongation and expansion during development.
evidence: This is a summary of the study's contributions stated in the discussion.

claim: Col2a1-CreER:R26R-Confetti heterozygous mice were generated by crossing mice homozygous for Col2-CreERT with R26R-Confetti homozygotes.
source: For genetic labeling of chondrocyte clones in embryonic and postnatal growth plates, Col2a1-CreER:R26R-Confetti heterozygous mice were generated by crossing mice homozygous for Col2-CreERT (Jackson Laboratories, FVB-Tg (Col2a1-cre/ERT)KA3Smac/J; Nakamura et al., 2006) with R26R-Confetti homozygotes (Jackson Laboratories, B6.129P2-Gt(ROSA)26Sortm1(CAG-Brainbow2.1)Cle/J; Snippert et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Tamoxifen was administered by oral gavage at a dose of 3 mg to P30 Col2a1-CreER:R26R-Confetti+/-mice or 2 mg to time-mated R26R-Confetti females at E14.5.
source: For clonal genetic tracing, tamoxifen was administered by oral gavage (Fine Science Tools) at a dose of 3 mg to P30 Col2a1-CreER:R26R-Confetti+/-mice or 2 mg to time-mated R26R-Confetti females at E14.5.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Neighboring cells that expressed the same fluorescent protein were considered clonal.
source: Neighboring cells that expressed the same fluorescent protein were considered clonal.
evidence: This is a description of the experimental method stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: A 200-µm-thick section contains 5–6 cells in thickness in the PZ and 2–3 cells in the HZ.
source: A 200-µm-thick section contains 5–6 cells in thickness in the PZ and 2–3 cells in the HZ.
evidence: This is a description of the sample characteristics stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Nuclear centroids can be used as a proxy for cell centroids.
source: To evaluate whether nuclear centroids can be used as a proxy for cell centroids, we performed correlation analysis on our previously published dataset of a wild-type tibia sample (Rubin et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a methodological validation stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The Pearson correlation between the mean elevation angle in a clone based on either cell or nuclear centroids was 0.79.
source: Additionally, we computed the Pearson correlation between the mean elevation angle in a clone based on either cell or nuclear centroids, resulting in a correlation value of 0.79 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from correlation analysis stated in the Materials and methods section and shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 2B.

claim: Elevation angle calculation performed on nuclei can serve as a reliable proxy for cell-based measurements.
source: These results suggest that elevation angle calculation performed on nuclei can serve as a reliable proxy for cell-based measurements.
evidence: This is a conclusion from the correlation analysis stated in the Materials and methods section.
